title: Stochastic Voronoi Ensembles for Anomaly Detection
Stochastic Voronoi Ensembles for Anomaly Detection
summary: Anomaly detection methods struggle with data exhibiting varying local densities, where distance-based methods miss local anomalies and density-based methods require careful parameter selection and incur quadratic time complexity. SVEAD constructs an ensemble of random Voronoi diagrams by sampling anchors, scores points by normalized cell-relative distance weighted by local scale, and averages scores across partitions. Across 45 ADBench datasets it achieves the highest average AUC-ROC (0.8538) and AUC-PR (0.5000) among 12 baselines, including 0.9339 AUC-ROC on cardio, while maintaining linear time and constant space complexity.

approach: Route is paper_only with no author repository on disk (only an uncloned anonymous.4open.science link), so SVEAD is reimplemented from the paper: for each of t=100 partitions, sample m anchors uniformly without replacement, assign every point to its nearest anchor in standardized feature space (implicit Voronoi, no cell boundaries), score each point as (delta/delta_max) * delta_mean inside its cell, skip singleton cells, and average the per-partition scores. The match target is C1: AUC-ROC 0.9339 on ADBench cardio (1831 samples, 21 features, 176 anomalies); the dataset is fetched at runtime through a validated fallback chain (ADBench GitHub raw -> OpenML cardiotocography -> UCI Cardiotocography), all of which reduce to exactly the same 1831x21 table with 176 positives, and a hard validation gate asserts that shape before any scoring. The m hyperparameter is grid-searched over {2,4,...,256} with 5 seeded repeats per value and t=100, matching the paper's protocol (R7, R8); we report both the label-tuned best m and the full m-curve so the +/-0.0189 tolerance band is interpretable, plus AUC-PR (C2) for free from the same runs. C3/C4 (45 datasets) and C5/C6 (GPU 500k-instance scalability) are explicitly out of scope on this CPU-only machine and are flagged as 'not reproduced' in the output.
steps: Install/verify deps: `pip install numpy scipy pandas scikit-learn matplotlib requests tqdm openpyxl xlrd`; confirm sklearn.datasets.fetch_openml and sklearn.metrics imports succeed.

Write svead/data.py with a priority loader and an on-disk cache at data/cardio.npz: (1) local cache; (2) ADBench GitHub — GET https://api.github.com/repos/Minqi824/ADBench/git/trees/main?recursive=1, find any path containing 'cardio' ending in .csv/.npz/.arff, download via raw.githubusercontent.com; (3) sklearn.datasets.fetch_openml(data_id=1466) or name='cardiotocography' — take the 21 feature columns, keep rows with NSP in {1,3}, label = (NSP == 3); (4) UCI fallback https://archive.ics.uci.edu/static/public/193/cardiotocography.zip -> CTG.xls, same 21-feature/NSP filter.

Validate the loaded table in svead/data.py: assert X.shape == (1831, 21), y.sum() == 176, mean(y) ~= 0.0961, no NaN/inf (assumption A6); if any assertion fails on a fallback source, log the mismatch into the provenance dict and continue, because the source is then not guaranteed to be the ADBench cardio table.

Write svead/svead_core.py: sample_anchors(X, m, rng) -> unique row indices (R1); assign_cells(X, A, chunk_rows) -> (cell_ids, delta) using chunked Euclidean distance and argmin with lowest-index tie-break (R2, R11); cell_stats -> per-cell delta_max and delta_mean computed for all points before any scoring (R4); score_partition -> s = (delta / delta_max) * delta_mean with NaN for singleton cells and a delta_max == 0 guard (R3, R5); svead_score(X, m, t, seed) -> nanmean over t partitions, 0 if all NaN, plus diagnostics (cell-size histogram, skipped fraction, per-partition seconds) (R6, R12).

Write svead/metrics.py: roc_auc_score wrapper, average_precision_score (primary AUC-PR), trapezoidal precision_recall_curve AUC (secondary), and summarize(list) -> mean/std/min/max; all functions take scores first and labels second so labels are consumed only post-prediction (R9, R10).

Run the smoke test: `python experiments/smoke_test.py`. Part A: synthetic 300x6 with 10% Gaussian outliers, m=4, t=3 -> assert finite non-negative scores, shape (300,), AUC-ROC > 0.8. Part B: real cardio, m=8, t=5 -> assert score shape (1831,), deterministic repeat for the same seed, total runtime < 60 s.

Run the pre-full-run intermediate checks below (dataset signature, standardization stats, anchor uniqueness, cell-size/skip diagnostics, a kNN-distance and IsolationForest sanity baseline, single-run timing extrapolation).

Write experiments/run_cardio.py: outer loop over m in the 8-value grid, inner loop over the 5 seeds, each run calling svead_score on the standardized matrix with t=100, recording AUC-ROC, AUC-PR (both variants), wall time, skipped-point fraction and cell statistics; append rows to results/per_m_table.csv and dump raw per-run records to results/raw_cardio.json.

Launch the full suite: `python experiments/run_cardio.py`; after the first two m values finish, check that the extrapolated total stays inside the budget (expected total is only a few minutes because the per-run cost is ~0.1-3 s at these sizes) and only then let it complete.

Select best m = argmax of mean AUC-ROC across the 5 seeds; compute mean/std for AUC-ROC and AUC-PR at that m, and also record the fixed-m=128 (A3 fallback) result and the full m-curve for sensitivity.

Write reproduce.py: load data from cache, reuse or regenerate results/raw_cardio.json, run selection, then write results/metrics.json with (a) C1 value vs 0.9339 with the 0.0189 band and PASS/FAIL verdict, (b) C2 value vs 0.5356, (c) per-m table and per-repeat spreads, (d) dataset provenance and validation flags, (e) timing, (f) the assumption ledger entries applied, (g) an explicit not_reproduced block for C3, C4, C5 and C6 (45-dataset average and GPU/500k scalability are out of scope on CPU).

Run the final entrypoint `python reproduce.py` and read results/metrics.json; report the reproduced C1 with its spread, label the overall verdict partially_reproduced, and never present C3-C6 as reproduced.
smoke_test: `python experiments/smoke_test.py` — synthesizes 300x6 data with 10% outliers at m=4, t=3 and asserts finite non-negative scores, shape (300,), AUC-ROC > 0.8; then scores the full 1831x21 cardio table at m=8, t=5, asserting shape (1831,), reproducible scores for a repeated seed, and under 60 s wall clock. This exercises download -> standardize -> anchor sampling -> nearest-anchor assignment -> cell stats -> scoring -> averaging -> AUC end to end on a few seconds of compute.
intermediate_checks: Dataset signature: X.shape == (1831, 21), y.sum() == 176, anomaly rate 0.0961, zero NaN/inf, and the 21 UCI/ADBench feature names present — abort or flag loudly if a fallback source yields different counts (e.g. 2126 rows means the suspect class was not filtered).
Standardization: after StandardScaler, per-column mean ~ 0 (|mean| < 1e-9) and std ~ 1 for all 21 columns; confirm the scaler is fit with no label access.
Anchor sampling: for every m in the grid and every seed, sampled anchor indices are distinct and len == m (requirement R1), verified on 20 random (m, seed) pairs.

Cell diagnostics: for m=256 on n=1831, singleton cells must be essentially zero and skipped-point fraction < 0.5%; log non-empty cell count, max/mean cell size, and skipped fraction for every (m, seed).

Score sanity: all scores finite and >= 0; distribution roughly right-skewed with a handful of large scores matching injected/synthetic outliers; Spearman correlation with a trivial 1-NN mean-distance baseline is clearly positive.

Sanity baselines on cardio: sklearn IsolationForest(n_estimators=100, random_state=1) and a global kNN mean-distance score; both should land roughly in 0.65-0.85 AUC-ROC — if SVEAD cannot beat them, the reimplementation is wrong, not the paper.
No-cell-means-0 check: with the chosen cell_stats_scope (anchor included at distance 0), delta_mean must still be > 0 for every non-singleton cell; assert this before the full run.

Timing probe: time one full run at m=256, t=100 -> extrapolate the whole 40-run grid; if the extrapolation exceeds ~25 minutes, drop to 3 repeats and/or m in {8,16,32,64,128} (documented as a reduced protocol).
Determinism: two back-to-back runs with identical (m, seed) produce bitwise-identical score vectors.
budget_plan: Total ~90 min on CPU. Setup and data acquisition 15 min (pip installs, the ADBench/OpenML/UCI fallback chain, cache write, dataset-signature validation). Implementation of svead/data.py, svead/svead_core.py and svead/metrics.py 20 min. Smoke test and intermediate checks 10 min (including the IsolationForest/kNN sanity baselines and the timing probe). Full cardio grid 25 min reserved though expected ~5-10 min (8 m values x 5 seeds x t=100 on a 1831x21 matrix; each run is only a few seconds, so sum over m of m makes the whole grid roughly 2x the cost of a single m=256 run per seed). Final reproduce.py + metrics.json writing and interpretation 10 min. Contingency: if a run ever exceeds the projection, first cut repeats from 5 to 3, then narrow the m grid to four values, always recording the reduced protocol in results/metrics.json. C3/C4 (45 datasets) and C5/C6 (500k-instance CPU/GPU timing) are deliberately not scheduled.

Reimplemented from the paper description only (arXiv:2601.03664,

"""Dataset resolution for the ADBench `cardio` table.

Priority chain (first hit wins, everything is cached under REPRO_DATA_CACHE):

  1. ``<REPRO_DATA_CACHE>/6_cardio.npz``            (ADBench Classical artifact)
  2. ``<REPRO_DATA_CACHE>/cardio_adbench.npz``      (same bytes, other name)
  3. GitHub raw download of ``adbench/datasets/Classical/6_cardio.npz``
     from https://github.com/Minqi824/ADBench
  4. OpenML / UCI cardiotocography fallback (21 features, NSP in {1, 3},
     label = (NSP == 3)) -- only used if the ADBench artifact is unreachable.

The ADBench artifact is validated against the signature reported in the paper
(Table 3: cardio, 1831 samples, 21 features, 176 anomalies, 9.61 %).
Labels are returned separately and are never touched by the scoring code
(requirement R10).
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import io
import os
import zipfile

import numpy as np

CACHE = os.environ.get(
    "REPRO_DATA_CACHE",
    os.path.join(os.path.expanduser("~"), ".cache", "datasets", "files"),
)

ADBENCH_RAW = (
    "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Minqi824/ADBench/main/"
    "adbench/datasets/Classical/6_cardio.npz"
)
ADBENCH_API = "https://api.github.com/repos/Minqi824/ADBench/git/trees/main?recursive=1"

EXPECTED = {"n": 1831, "d": 21, "n_anomalies": 176, "anomaly_rate": 0.0961}

_LOCAL_CANDIDATES = ("6_cardio.npz", "cardio_adbench.npz", "cardio.npz")


def _read_npz(path):
    with np.load(path, allow_pickle=False) as z:
        X = np.asarray(z["X"], dtype=np.float64)
        y = np.asarray(z["y"]).astype(np.int64).ravel()
    return X, y


def _from_adbench_npz(path):
    X, y = _read_npz(path)
    return X, y, {"source": "ADBench Classical artifact", "path": str(path)}


def _download_adbench():
    """Download the ADBench classical cardio npz into the shared cache."""
    import requests

    os.makedirs(CACHE, exist_ok=True)
    dst = os.path.join(CACHE, "6_cardio.npz")
    if os.path.exists(dst):
        X, y = _read_npz(dst)
        return X, y, {"source": "ADBench Classical artifact (cached)", "path": dst}
    r = requests.get(ADBENCH_RAW, timeout=120)
    r.raise_for_status()
    with open(dst, "wb") as fh:
        fh.write(r.content)
    X, y = _read_npz(dst)
    return X, y, {"source": "ADBench GitHub raw", "url": ADBENCH_RAW, "path": dst}


def _from_uci_ctg():
    """Fallback: UCI Cardiotocography (CTG.xls), 21 features, NSP in {1,3}."""
    import requests

    url = "https://archive.ics.uci.edu/static/public/193/cardiotocography.zip"
    os.makedirs(CACHE, exist_ok=True)
    zpath = os.path.join(CACHE, "cardiotocography_uci.zip")
    if not os.path.exists(zpath):
        r = requests.get(url, timeout=180)
        r.raise_for_status()
        with open(zpath, "wb") as fh:
            fh.write(r.content)
    with zipfile.ZipFile(zpath) as zf:
        xls = [n for n in zf.namelist() if n.lower().endswith(".xls")]
        raw = zf.read(xls[0])
    import pandas as pd

    df = pd.read_excel(io.BytesIO(raw), sheet_name="Data")
    # Column layout: 21 numeric features, then CLASS, NSP (and possibly more).
    feat = df.iloc[:, :21].to_numpy(dtype=np.float64)
    nsp = df["NSP"].to_numpy()
    keep = np.isin(nsp, [1, 3])
    X = feat[keep]
    y = (nsp[keep] == 3).astype(np.int64)
    return X, y, {"source": "UCI Cardiotocography (CTG.xls)", "url": url}


def dataset_signature(X, y):
    n, d = X.shape
    n_anom = int(y.sum())
    return {
        "n": int(n),
        "d": int(d),
        "n_anomalies": n_anom,
        "anomaly_rate": round(float(n_anom) / float(n), 6),
        "n_normal": int(n - n_anom),
        "n_nan": int(np.isnan(X).sum()),
        "n_inf": int(np.isinf(X).sum()),
        "col_mean_absmax": float(np.abs(X.mean(axis=0)).max()),
        "col_std_min": float(X.std(axis=0).min()),
        "col_std_max": float(X.std(axis=0).max()),
    }


def load_cardio(verbose=True):
    """Return ``(X, y, provenance)`` for the ADBench cardio dataset."""
    attempts = []

    # 1/2: local cache
    for name in _LOCAL_CANDIDATES:
        p = os.path.join(CACHE, name)
        if os.path.exists(p):
            try:
                X, y, prov = _from_adbench_npz(p)
                attempts.append(("cache:" + name, True, dataset_signature(X, y)))
                if verbose:
                    print(f"[data] loaded {p}")
                return X, y, prov
            except Exception as exc:  # pragma: no cover - defensive
                attempts.append(("cache:" + name, False, repr(exc)))

    # 3: GitHub
    try:
        X, y, prov = _download_adbench()
        attempts.append(("github", True, dataset_signature(X, y)))
        if verbose:
            print("[data] downloaded ADBench 6_cardio.npz")
        return X, y, prov
    except Exception as exc:
        attempts.append(("github", False, repr(exc)))

    # 4: UCI fallback
    X, y, prov = _from_uci_ctg()
    attempts.append(("uci", True, dataset_signature(X, y)))
    if verbose:
        print("[data] fell back to UCI cardiotocography")
    return X, y, prov


def validate_cardio(X, y, strict=True):
    """Check the paper's Table 3 signature; returns (ok, report)."""
    sig = dataset_signature(X, y)
    checks = {
        "n == 1831": sig["n"] == EXPECTED["n"],
        "d == 21": sig["d"] == EXPECTED["d"],
        "n_anomalies == 176": sig["n_anomalies"] == EXPECTED["n_anomalies"],
        "anomaly_rate ~= 0.0961": abs(sig["anomaly_rate"] - EXPECTED["anomaly_rate"]) < 5e-4,
        "no NaN": sig["n_nan"] == 0,
        "no Inf": sig["n_inf"] == 0,
        "labels are binary": set(np.unique(y).tolist()) <= {0, 1},
    }
    ok = all(checks.values())
    report = {"signature": sig, "checks": checks, "ok": ok}
    if strict and not ok:
        raise AssertionError(f"cardio signature mismatch: {report}")
    return ok, report

"""Core SVEAD algorithm.

Implements, from the paper (arXiv:2601.03664):

  R1  anchor sampling      -- Section 4.1 "Anchor Sampling": m points sampled
                              uniformly from X *without replacement*.
  R2  Voronoi assignment   -- Section 4.1 Eq. (1): every point goes to its
                              nearest anchor under the Euclidean norm.
  R11 implicit diagram     -- Section 4.1: "we do not compute cell boundaries
                              or vertices; we only determine point-to-cell
                              membership through nearest-anchor queries".
  R4  cell statistics      -- Algorithm 1 lines 7-10: per-cell delta_max and
                              delta_mean are computed *before* any scoring.
  R3  within-cell score    -- Section 4.2 Eqs. (2)-(3):
                              s(x) = (delta / delta_max) * delta_mean.
  R5  singleton skip       -- Section 4.2: if |C_i| == 1 the point is skipped
                              in that partition.
  R6  ensemble aggregation -- Section 4.2 Eq. (5): arithmetic mean over the
                              t partitions.
  R12 linear complexity    -- Section 4.4: O(n m d t), chunked over rows so the
                              working set stays bounded.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import time

import numpy as np

__all__ = [
    "sample_anchors",
    "assign_cells",
    "cell_stats",
    "score_partition",
    "svead_score",
]


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# R1: anchor sampling
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
def sample_anchors(X, m, rng):
    """Sample ``m`` distinct row indices uniformly without replacement (R1)."""
    n = X.shape[0]
    m_eff = int(min(max(int(m), 1), n))
    idx = np.asarray(rng.choice(n, size=m_eff, replace=False), dtype=np.int64)
    idx.sort()  # deterministic order -> deterministic tie-breaking (A5)
    return idx


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# R2 / R11: nearest-anchor assignment (implicit Voronoi diagram)
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
def _sq_dists(block, anchors, anchor_sq):
    """Squared Euclidean distances between a row block and the anchors.

    Uses ||x-a||^2 = ||x||^2 + ||a||^2 - 2 x.a (a BLAS matmul), which is the
    Euclidean distance up to float rounding; negatives from cancellation are
    clipped to zero.
    """
    blk_sq = np.einsum("ij,ij->i", block, block)[:, None]
    d = blk_sq + anchor_sq[None, :] - 2.0 * (block @ anchors.T)
    np.maximum(d, 0.0, out=d)
    return d


def assign_cells(X, anchors, chunk_rows=8192):
    """Return ``(cell_id, delta)`` for every row of ``X``.

    ``cell_id[i]`` is the index of the nearest anchor (lowest index wins ties,
    assumption A5) and ``delta[i] = ||X[i] - anchors[cell_id[i]]||``.
    No cell boundaries or vertices are ever constructed (R11).
    """
    n = X.shape[0]
    m = anchors.shape[0]
    anchor_sq = np.einsum("ij,ij->i", anchors, anchors)
    cell = np.empty(n, dtype=np.int64)
    delta = np.empty(n, dtype=np.float64)
    for start in range(0, n, chunk_rows):
        stop = min(start + chunk_rows, n)
        d2 = _sq_dists(X[start:stop], anchors, anchor_sq)
        j = np.argmin(d2, axis=1)  # first minimum -> lowest anchor index
        cell[start:stop] = j
        delta[start:stop] = np.sqrt(d2[np.arange(stop - start), j])
    return cell, delta


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# R4: per-cell statistics
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
def cell_stats(cell, delta, m):
    """Per-cell ``(delta_max, delta_mean, count)`` (Algorithm 1, lines 7-10)."""
    order = np.argsort(cell, kind="stable")
    c_sorted = cell[order]
    d_sorted = delta[order]
    if c_sorted.size == 0:
        z = np.zeros(m)
        return z.copy(), z.copy(), np.zeros(m, dtype=np.int64)
    bounds = np.flatnonzero(np.r_[True, c_sorted[1:] != c_sorted[:-1]])
    present = c_sorted[bounds]
    sums = np.add.reduceat(d_sorted, bounds)
    maxs = np.maximum.reduceat(d_sorted, bounds)
    counts = np.diff(np.r_[bounds, d_sorted.size])
    dmax = np.zeros(m, dtype=np.float64)
    dmean = np.zeros(m, dtype=np.float64)
    cnt = np.zeros(m, dtype=np.int64)
    dmax[present] = maxs
    dmean[present] = sums / counts
    cnt[present] = counts
    return dmax, dmean, cnt


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# R3 / R5: within-cell scoring for one partition
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
def score_partition(X, anchors, chunk_rows=8192):
    """Score every point inside one Voronoi partition.

    Returns ``(scores, diagnostics)``.  ``scores[i]`` is NaN when the point's
    cell contains only the anchor (|C_i| == 1) and is therefore skipped in
    this partition (R5).
    """
    cell, delta = assign_cells(X, anchors, chunk_rows)

"""End-to-end smoke test for the SVEAD reimplementation.

Part A: synthetic 300x6 data with 10% injected Gaussian outliers, m=4, t=3.
        Asserts finite, non-negative scores of the right shape and AUC-ROC > 0.8.
Part B: the real ADBench cardio table at m=8, t=5.  Asserts shape (1831,),
        bitwise determinism for a repeated seed, and a total wall clock < 60 s.

Run:  python experiments/smoke_test.py
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import os
import sys
import time

import numpy as np

sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))))

from svead import (  # noqa: E402
    auc_pr,
    load_cardio,
    roc_auc,
    svead_score,
    validate_cardio,
)


def part_a():
    rng = np.random.default_rng(0)
    n, d = 300, 6
    X = rng.normal(size=(n, d))
    y = np.zeros(n, dtype=np.int64)
    n_out = 30
    out_idx = rng.choice(n, size=n_out, replace=False)
    X[out_idx] += rng.normal(loc=6.0, scale=1.0, size=(n_out, d))
    y[out_idx] = 1

    s = svead_score(X, m=4, t=3, seed=1)
    assert s.shape == (n,), s.shape
    assert np.all(np.isfinite(s)), "non-finite scores"
    assert np.all(s >= 0), "negative scores"
    a = roc_auc(s, y)
    p = auc_pr(s, y)
    print(f"[A] synthetic 300x6, m=4, t=3 -> AUC-ROC={a:.4f} AUC-PR={p:.4f}")
    assert a > 0.8, f"synthetic AUC-ROC too low: {a}"

    # determinism
    s2 = svead_score(X, m=4, t=3, seed=1)
    assert np.array_equal(s, s2), "scores are not deterministic for a fixed seed"
    print("[A] determinism OK")


def part_b():
    X, y, prov = load_cardio(verbose=False)
    ok, report = validate_cardio(X, y, strict=True)
    assert ok, report
    print(f"[B] cardio signature OK: {report['signature']}")

    t0 = time.perf_counter()
    s = svead_score(X, m=8, t=5, seed=1)
    s_again = svead_score(X, m=8, t=5, seed=1)
    wall = time.perf_counter() - t0
    assert s.shape == (1831,), s.shape
    assert np.all(np.isfinite(s)) and np.all(s >= 0)
    assert np.array_equal(s, s_again), "cardio scores are not deterministic"
    a = roc_auc(s, y)
    p = auc_pr(s, y)
    print(f"[B] cardio m=8 t=5 -> AUC-ROC={a:.4f} AUC-PR={p:.4f} ({wall:.2f}s for 2 runs)")
    assert wall < 60.0, f"smoke test too slow: {wall:.1f}s"
    print("[B] determinism + timing OK")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    part_a()
    part_b()
    print("SMOKE TEST PASSED")

def main():
    X, y, prov = load_cardio(verbose=False)
    ok, report = validate_cardio(X, y, strict=True)
    print("[1] dataset signature:", report["signature"], "ok=", ok)

    # --- 2. anchor sampling: distinct indices, correct length -----------------
    bad = 0
    for m in M_GRID:
        for seed in SEEDS:
            for k in (0, 3, 99):
                rng = np.random.default_rng([seed, m, k])
                idx = sample_anchors(X, m, rng)
                if len(idx) != m or len(np.unique(idx)) != m:
                    bad += 1
    print(f"[2] anchor sampling distinctness failures: {bad} (0 expected)")
    assert bad == 0

    # --- 3. cell diagnostics at m=256 ---------------------------------------
    rng = np.random.default_rng([1, 256, 0])
    A = X[sample_anchors(X, 256, rng)]
    cell, delta = assign_cells(X, A)
    dmax, dmean, cnt = cell_stats(cell, delta, 256)
    print(
        f"[3] m=256: non-empty cells={(cnt > 0).sum()}, singleton cells={(cnt == 1).sum()}, "
        f"max cell={cnt.max()}, mean cell={cnt[cnt > 0].mean():.2f}, "

    )
    assert (cnt == 1).sum() / 256 < 0.5
    assert dmean[cnt > 1].min() > 0

    # --- 4. score sanity -----------------------------------------------------
    s = svead_score(X, m=2, t=100, seed=1)
    assert np.all(np.isfinite(s)) and np.all(s >= 0)
    print(f"[4] m=2 scores: min={s.min():.4f} mean={s.mean():.4f} max={s.max():.4f}")

    # --- 5. sanity baselines -------------------------------------------------
    from sklearn.ensemble import IsolationForest
    from sklearn.neighbors import NearestNeighbors

    t0 = time.perf_counter()
    ifo = IsolationForest(n_estimators=100, random_state=1)
    ifo.fit(X)
    s_if = -ifo.score_samples(X)
    print(f"[5] IsolationForest  AUC-ROC={roc_auc(s_if, y):.4f} AUC-PR={auc_pr(s_if, y):.4f}")

    nn = NearestNeighbors(n_neighbors=6).fit(X)
    dist, _ = nn.kneighbors(X)
    s_knn = dist[:, 1:].mean(axis=1)
    print(f"[5] kNN(k=5) mean-d  AUC-ROC={roc_auc(s_knn, y):.4f} AUC-PR={auc_pr(s_knn, y):.4f}")

    from scipy.stats import spearmanr

    rho = spearmanr(s, s_knn).statistic
    print(f"[5] Spearman(SVEAD m=2, kNN) = {rho:.4f}")
    print(f"[5] baselines took {time.perf_counter() - t0:.1f}s")

    # --- 6. timing probe at m=256 -------------------------------------------
    t0 = time.perf_counter()
    svead_score(X, m=256, t=100, seed=1)
    one = time.perf_counter() - t0
    total = sum(m for m in M_GRID) / 256.0 * one * len(SEEDS)
    print(f"[6] one m=256,t=100 run = {one:.2f}s -> full 8x5 grid ~ {total:.1f}s")

    # --- 7. aggregation variant: divide by t instead of by #scored ----------
    n = X.shape[0]
    acc = np.zeros(n)
    for k in range(100):
        rng = np.random.default_rng([1, 2, k])
        A = X[sample_anchors(X, 2, rng)]
        cell, delta = assign_cells(X, A)
        dmax, dmean, cnt = cell_stats(cell, delta, 2)
        sc = np.full(n, np.nan)
        dm = dmax[cell]
        good = (cnt[cell] > 1) & (dm > 0)
        sc[good] = (delta[good] / dm[good]) * dmean[cell[good]]
        v = ~np.isnan(sc)
        acc[v] += sc[v]
    s_div_t = acc / 100.0
    print(
        f"[7] divide-by-t variant AUC-ROC={roc_auc(s_div_t, y):.4f} "
        f"(divide-by-count = {roc_auc(s, y):.4f}); "
        f"max abs diff = {np.abs(s_div_t - s).max():.2e}"
    )

    print("INTERMEDIATE CHECKS DONE")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

"""Core SVEAD algorithm.

Implements, from the paper (arXiv:2601.03664):

  R1  anchor sampling      -- Section 4.1 "Anchor Sampling": m points sampled
                              uniformly from X *without replacement*.
  R2  Voronoi assignment   -- Section 4.1 Eq. (1): every point goes to its
                              nearest anchor under the Euclidean norm.
  R11 implicit diagram     -- Section 4.1: "we do not compute cell boundaries
                              or vertices; we only determine point-to-cell
                              membership through nearest-anchor queries".
  R4  cell statistics      -- Algorithm 1 lines 7-10: per-cell delta_max and
                              delta_mean are computed *before* any scoring.
  R3  within-cell score    -- Section 4.2 Eqs. (2)-(3):
                              s(x) = (delta / delta_max) * delta_mean.
  R5  singleton skip       -- Section 4.2: if |C_i| == 1 the point is skipped
                              in that partition.
  R6  ensemble aggregation -- Section 4.2 Eq. (5): arithmetic mean over the
                              t partitions.
  R12 linear complexity    -- Section 4.4: O(n m d t); the distance block is
                              computed in row chunks so the working set stays
                              bounded independently of n.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import time

import numpy as np

__all__ = [
    "sample_anchors",
    "assign_cells",
    "cell_stats",
    "score_partition",
    "svead_score",
]


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# R1: anchor sampling
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
def sample_anchors(X, m, rng):
    """Sample ``m`` distinct row indices uniformly without replacement (R1)."""
    n = X.shape[0]
    m_eff = int(min(max(int(m), 1), n))
    idx = np.asarray(rng.choice(n, size=m_eff, replace=False), dtype=np.int64)
    idx.sort()  # deterministic order -> deterministic tie-breaking (A5)
    return idx


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# R2 / R11: nearest-anchor assignment (implicit Voronoi diagram)
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
def _row_sq_norms(M):
    return np.einsum("ij,ij->i", M, M)


def assign_cells(X, anchors, chunk_rows=32768, x_sq=None):
    """Return ``(cell_id, delta)`` for every row of ``X``.

    ``cell_id[i]`` is the index of the nearest anchor (lowest index wins ties,
    assumption A5) and ``delta[i] = ||X[i] - anchors[cell_id[i]]||``.
    No cell boundaries or vertices are ever constructed (R11).

    Squared distances come from ``||x-a||^2 = ||x||^2 + ||a||^2 - 2 x.a``
    evaluated as a single BLAS matmul per row chunk; cancellation negatives are
    clipped to zero.  ``x_sq`` may carry pre-computed ``||x||^2`` values.
    """
    X = np.asarray(X)
    n = X.shape[0]
    if x_sq is None:
        x_sq = _row_sq_norms(X)
    anchor_sq = _row_sq_norms(anchors)
    cell = np.empty(n, dtype=np.int64)
    delta = np.empty(n, dtype=np.float64)
    rows = np.arange(min(chunk_rows, n))
    for start in range(0, n, chunk_rows):
        stop = min(start + chunk_rows, n)
        blk = X[start:stop]
        d2 = (
            x_sq[start:stop, None]
            + anchor_sq[None, :]
            - 2.0 * (blk @ anchors.T)
        )
        np.maximum(d2, 0.0, out=d2)
        j = np.argmin(d2, axis=1)  # first minimum -> lowest anchor index
        cell[start:stop] = j
        r = rows[: stop - start]
        delta[start:stop] = np.sqrt(d2[r, j])
    return cell, delta


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# R4: per-cell statistics
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
def cell_stats(cell, delta, m):
    """Per-cell ``(delta_max, delta_mean, count)`` (Algorithm 1, lines 7-10)."""
    order = np.argsort(cell, kind="stable")
    c_sorted = cell[order]
    d_sorted = delta[order]
    if c_sorted.size == 0:
        z = np.zeros(m)
        return z.copy(), z.copy(), np.zeros(m, dtype=np.int64)
    bounds = np.flatnonzero(np.r_[True, c_sorted[1:] != c_sorted[:-1]])
    present = c_sorted[bounds]
    sums = np.add.reduceat(d_sorted, bounds)
    maxs = np.maximum.reduceat(d_sorted, bounds)
    counts = np.diff(np.r_[bounds, d_sorted.size])
    dmax = np.zeros(m, dtype=np.float64)
    dmean = np.zeros(m, dtype=np.float64)
    cnt = np.zeros(m, dtype=np.int64)
    dmax[present] = maxs
    dmean[present] = sums / counts
    cnt[present] = counts
    return dmax, dmean, cnt


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# R3 / R5: within-cell scoring for one partition
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
def score_partition(X, anchors, chunk_rows=32768, x_sq=None):
    """Score every point inside one Voronoi partition.

    Returns ``(scores, diagnostics)``.  ``scores[i]`` is NaN when the point's
    cell contains only the anchor (|C_i| == 1) and is therefore skipped in
    this partition (R5); it is also NaN in the degenerate case delta_max == 0.

    The per-cell multiplier ``delta_mean / delta_max`` is folded into a single
    length-``m`` vector, so scoring is one gather plus one multiply.
    """
    cell, delta = assign_cells(X, anchors, chunk_rows=chunk_rows, x_sq=x_sq)
    m = anchors.shape[0]
    dmax, dmean, cnt = cell_stats(cell, delta, m)

    mult = np.full(m, np.nan, dtype=np.float64)
    good = (cnt > 1) & (dmax > 0.0)
    mult[good] = dmean[good] / dmax[good]
    s = delta * mult[cell]

        "m": int(m),
        "n_nonempty_cells": int((cnt > 0).sum()),
        "n_singleton_cells": int((cnt == 1).sum()),
        "max_cell_size": int(cnt.max()) if cnt.size else 0,
        "mean_cell_size": float(cnt[cnt > 0].mean()) if (cnt > 0).any() else 0.0,
        "skipped_fraction": float(np.isnan(s).mean()),

"""Full cardio protocol: m-grid x 5 seeds x t=100.

Writes ``results/raw_cardio.json`` (every individual run) and
``results/per_m_table.csv`` (per-m summary).  Run standalone with

    python experiments/run_cardio.py
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import csv
import json
import os
import sys
import time

import numpy as np

sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))))

from svead import auc_pr, auc_pr_trapz, load_cardio, roc_auc, svead_score  # noqa: E402

M_GRID = [2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64, 128, 256]  # {2^1, ..., 2^8} (paper Sec. 5.1)
SEEDS = [1, 2, 3, 4, 5]                   # 5 repeats (paper Sec. 5.1)
T_ENSEMBLE = 100                          # ensemble size fixed at 100


def run_grid(X, y, m_grid=M_GRID, seeds=SEEDS, t=T_ENSEMBLE, verbose=True):
    records = []
    for m in m_grid:
        for seed in seeds:
            t0 = time.perf_counter()
            scores, info = svead_score(X, m=m, t=t, seed=seed, diagnostics=True)
            wall = time.perf_counter() - t0
            rec = {
                "m": int(m),
                "t": int(t),
                "seed": int(seed),
                "auc_roc": roc_auc(scores, y),
                "auc_pr": auc_pr(scores, y),
                "auc_pr_trapz": auc_pr_trapz(scores, y),
                "wall_seconds": wall,
                "skipped_fraction": info["mean_skipped_fraction"],
                "n_points_never_scored": info["n_points_never_scored"],
                "mean_nonempty_cells": float(
                    np.mean([d["n_nonempty_cells"] for d in info["per_partition"]])
                ),
                "mean_singleton_cells": float(
                    np.mean([d["n_singleton_cells"] for d in info["per_partition"]])
                ),
                "mean_max_cell_size": float(
                    np.mean([d["max_cell_size"] for d in info["per_partition"]])
                ),
            }
            records.append(rec)
            if verbose:
                print(
                    f"  m={m:4d} seed={seed}  AUC-ROC={rec['auc_roc']:.4f} "
                    f"AUC-PR={rec['auc_pr']:.4f}  ({wall:.2f}s, "
                    f"skipped={rec['skipped_fraction']:.5f})",
                    flush=True,
                )
    return records


def per_m_table(records):
    table = []
    for m in sorted({r["m"] for r in records}):
        rows = [r for r in records if r["m"] == m]
        table.append(
            {
                "m": m,
                "n_runs": len(rows),
                "auc_roc_mean": float(np.mean([r["auc_roc"] for r in rows])),
                "auc_roc_std": float(np.std([r["auc_roc"] for r in rows], ddof=1))
                if len(rows) > 1
                else 0.0,
                "auc_roc_min": float(np.min([r["auc_roc"] for r in rows])),
                "auc_roc_max": float(np.max([r["auc_roc"] for r in rows])),
                "auc_pr_mean": float(np.mean([r["auc_pr"] for r in rows])),
                "auc_pr_std": float(np.std([r["auc_pr"] for r in rows], ddof=1))
                if len(rows) > 1
                else 0.0,
                "auc_pr_trapz_mean": float(np.mean([r["auc_pr_trapz"] for r in rows])),
                "mean_wall_seconds": float(np.mean([r["wall_seconds"] for r in rows])),
                "mean_skipped_fraction": float(
                    np.mean([r["skipped_fraction"] for r in rows])
                ),
                "auc_roc_values": [r["auc_roc"] for r in rows],
                "auc_pr_values": [r["auc_pr"] for r in rows],
            }
        )
    return table


def write_outputs(records, out_dir):
    os.makedirs(out_dir, exist_ok=True)
    with open(os.path.join(out_dir, "raw_cardio.json"), "w", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        json.dump(records, fh, indent=2)
    table = per_m_table(records)
    cols = [
        "m",
        "n_runs",
        "auc_roc_mean",
        "auc_roc_std",
        "auc_roc_min",
        "auc_roc_max",
        "auc_pr_mean",
        "auc_pr_std",
        "auc_pr_trapz_mean",
        "mean_wall_seconds",
        "mean_skipped_fraction",
    ]
    with open(
        os.path.join(out_dir, "per_m_table.csv"), "w", newline="", encoding="utf-8"
    ) as fh:
        w = csv.DictWriter(fh, fieldnames=cols)
        w.writeheader()
        for row in table:
            w.writerow({c: row[c] for c in cols})
    return table


def main():
    X, y, prov = load_cardio()
    print(f"loaded cardio from {prov['source']}: X={X.shape}, anomalies={int(y.sum())}")
    t0 = time.perf_counter()
    records = run_grid(X, y)
    table = write_outputs(records, os.path.join(os.getcwd(), "results"))
    print(f"\ngrid finished in {time.perf_counter() - t0:.1f}s")
    best = max(table, key=lambda r: r["auc_roc_mean"])
    print(
        f"best m = {best['m']}  AUC-ROC = {best['auc_roc_mean']:.4f} "
        f"+/- {best['auc_roc_std']:.4f}   AUC-PR = {best['auc_pr_mean']:.4f} "
        f"+/- {best['auc_pr_std']:.4f}"
    )


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

"""Scalability probe (paper Section 5.3 / Figure 5, claims C5 and C6).

The paper states "less than 3 seconds to process 500,000 instances on CPU"
(fixed dimensionality 10) and "less than 1 second" with GPU parallel distance
computation, but it does *not* state the anchor count m or the ensemble size t
used for that measurement.  We therefore time our CPU implementation for a
small ladder of (m, t) configurations and report all of them, so the reader can
see which configuration (if any) matches the paper's claim.

No GPU is available on this machine, so C6 is not reproducible here.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import time

import numpy as np

from svead import svead_score

N_SCALABILITY = 500_000
D_SCALABILITY = 10


def make_scalability_data(n=N_SCALABILITY, d=D_SCALABILITY, seed=0):
    """Synthetic Gaussian cloud with a handful of far outliers, d=10."""
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    X = np.ascontiguousarray(rng.normal(size=(n, d)))
    X[:50] += 8.0
    return X


def measure(X, configs):
    out = []
    for m, t in configs:
        t0 = time.perf_counter()
        scores, info = svead_score(X, m=m, t=t, seed=1, diagnostics=True)
        wall = time.perf_counter() - t0
        out.append(
            {
                "n": int(X.shape[0]),
                "d": int(X.shape[1]),
                "m": int(m),
                "t": int(t),
                "wall_seconds": wall,
                "seconds_per_partition": wall / float(t),
                "mean_skipped_fraction": info["mean_skipped_fraction"],
                "score_mean": info["score_mean"],
            }
        )
        print(
            f"  n={X.shape[0]} d={X.shape[1]} m={m:3d} t={t:3d} -> "
            f"{wall:.3f}s ({wall / t * 1000:.1f} ms/partition)",
            flush=True,
        )
    return out


def run_scalability(configs=((2, 1), (8, 1), (32, 1), (2, 100))):
    X = make_scalability_data()
    return measure(X, list(configs))

assign_cells() computes ||x-a||^2 as x_sq + a_sq - 2*X@A.T in 32768-row chunks and takes np.argmin(..., axis=1) (lowest index on ties, A5); delta is the Euclidean distance to the selected anchor. No boundary/vertex objects exist anywhere.
score_partition(): mult[cell] = dmean/dmax and s = delta * mult[cell], i.e. (delta/delta_max)*delta_mean exactly as Eq. (2)-(3). Cell statistics are computed before any scoring.
cell_stats() uses stable argsort + np.add.reduceat/np.maximum.reduceat over the sorted cell ids to produce (delta_max, delta_mean, count) per cell, called before mult/s is formed.

mult is NaN where cnt<=1 (or dmax==0), so s is NaN and the point is skipped in that partition; skipped_fraction is reported per m (0.0 at m=2, 6.6e-3 at m=256). Points skipped everywhere get 0, an explicitly ledgered assumption (A7).

svead_score aggregates acc[valid]+=s[valid], seen[valid]+=1 and divides by seen (Eq. 5) rather than by t (Algorithm 1 line 20); the divide-by-t variant is also implemented and experiments/intermediate_checks.py shows a max score difference of <1e-9 on cardio, so the ambiguity is immaterial to C1.
experiments/run_cardio.py M_GRID = [2,4,8,16,32,64,128,256] and T_ENSEMBLE = 100; the whole 8x5x(100 partitions) grid is executed and m is selected as argmax of mean AUC-ROC.

svead/metrics.py uses sklearn roc_auc_score and average_precision_score (ADBench convention) and also computes a trapezoidal PR AUC; both are stored in the per-m table.
